defects_found_and_fixed_during_publicati.what: the repositories' text normalization (core.autocrlf=true + text attributes) rewrote CRLF to LF in the committed blobs: 328 of the packet files were published with EOL-converted content, so their sha256 did not match PACKET_MANIFEST.json
defects_found_and_fixed_during_publicati.how_found: not by a claim — by recomputing git blob ids for 3 spot-checked files against the remote API, seeing MISMATCH, then fetching the remote blob bytes and confirming the difference was exactly CRLF->LF
defects_found_and_fixed_during_publicati.fix: EVIDENCE/CNV-PIPD-LS-SP-20261015/.gitattributes with '* -text' inside the packet subtree + core.autocrlf=false repo-local + 'git add --renormalize' + a follow-up commit on both branches
defects_found_and_fixed_during_publicati.verification_after_fix: full 566-file blob comparison on both repos: 0 mismatches
defects_found_and_fixed_during_publicati.residual: none known; the attribute is committed with the packet so a re-clone keeps the exact bytes

defects_found_and_fixed_during_publicati.what: the first PIPD-LS-SP publication attempt committed nothing: git refused with 'empty ident name (for <@users.noreply.github.com>) not allowed' in that clone, yet the push still created the branch and the readback printed MATCH True
defects_found_and_fixed_during_publicati.how_found: reading the commit output instead of trusting the exit path
defects_found_and_fixed_during_publicati.fix: repo-local user.name/user.email set on the PIPD-LS-SP clone (RP-002 HGK <hgk-rp002@local>, the same identity the Fabric evidence branch uses), then commit + push + a real content check
defects_found_and_fixed_during_publicati.lesson_recorded: a ref-level MATCH proves only ref equality; it is never content evidence — verify the tree, not the ref
